title: Bquant – Novel script for batch quantification of LCMS data
author: Rožman, Petrović
materials: Here we present novel script for batch quantification of liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LCMS) data. The script developed in this work was applied to quantify emerging contaminants in several European (FP7&H2020) and national projects e.g. Transformer, Globaqua and TransformCoast working on outputs of different instrument control software e.g. ThermoScientific Xcalibur, AB Sciex Analyst. In addition to environmental studies, the script can be applied for any quantitative analysis of different compounds in e.g. metabolomic or toxicological studies [1], [2]. This simple script enables quantification of data sets in a batch mode and shortens processing time from 20 min (manual interpretation) to several seconds per data set. Errors in data analysis are reduced and data can be quickly re-analysed using different inputs.

Mass spectra processing is not performed by Bquant script. Component peak identification and integration have to be executed using instrument vendor software. All instrument control software performs these basic operations. Signals used for quantification (peak area) may represent the parent compound or more commonly the two most intense selected reaction monitoring transitions (in terms of peak area). Once integration is performed output should be saved as Microsoft Excel xlsx file(s). Outputs from Thermo Xcalibur Quan Browser, AB Sciex Analyst and custom prepared file are provided as an examples (can be downloaded as Supporting information). Two files should be generated: one containing data for the calibration curve (e.g. Calibration-Analyst.xlsx) and the other containing data of the analytes (e.g. Data-Analyst.xlsx). Of all parameters reported by integration, user must ensure that Excel files created contain columns and appropriate data listed in Table 1. In addition, input text file (input.txt) which contains instructions for the Bquant script should be provided. First row should include name of the output to be used i.e Analyst, Thermo or custom. Following five rows must contain (in this order): value of the square of the correlation coefficient e.g. 0.99, minimum number of points for constructing calibration curve, concentration of the internal standard, confidence interval e.g. 0.95 (for 95%) and True if y-intercept of the calibration curve is allowed (otherwise False). Input for analysis of Thermo Xcalibur data must include additional row with names of all compounds to be quantified in curly brackets e.g. {Azithromycin, Ciprofloxacin,…}.

steps.title: Prepare Excel and input files
steps.instruction: Perform peak integration in the instrument vendor software, export the peak‑area data to two Microsoft Excel .xlsx files (one for the calibration curve, e.g., Calibration‑Analyst.xlsx, and one for the sample analytes, e.g., Data‑Analyst.xlsx) and make sure the columns listed in Table 1 are present. Create an input.txt file where the first line is the instrument identifier (Analyst, Thermo or custom); the next five lines contain, in order: the squared correlation‑coefficient value (e.g., 0.99), the minimum number of points required for constructing the calibration curve, the concentration of the internal standard, the confidence‑interval value (e.g., 0.95 for 95 %), and “True” if the y‑intercept may be fitted or “False” otherwise. For Thermo Xcalibur data add an additional line with all compound names in curly brackets (e.g., {Azithromycin, Ciprofloxacin,…}).

substeps.instruction: Integrate peaks in vendor software and export peak‑area data.
Save calibration data as Calibration‑Analyst.xlsx and sample data as Data‑Analyst.xlsx.
Verify that the Excel files contain the columns required by Table 1.
Create input.txt with the required rows (instrument name, r²‑square, minimum points, internal‑standard concentration, confidence interval, y‑intercept flag, and optional compound list).

steps.title: Run Bquant script
steps.instruction: Install or launch Wolfram Mathematica version 8 or higher on a computer with at least 2 GB RAM. Copy the entire Bquant folder to a convenient location (e.g., D:\…\Bquant\). Open the notebook that corresponds to the instrument data (e.g., …\Bquant\Analyst\Bquant‑Analyst.nb) in Mathematica, ensure that the Calibration‑Analyst.xlsx, Data‑Analyst.xlsx and input.txt files are in the same directory and correctly formatted, then select Evaluation → Evaluate Notebook to start the batch processing of the LC‑MS data.

substeps.instruction: Copy the Bquant folder to a desired directory.
Open the appropriate .nb notebook in Mathematica.
Confirm that the calibration, data, and input files are present and correctly formatted.
Choose Evaluation → Evaluate Notebook to run the script.

steps.title: Apply internal‑standard calculations
steps.instruction: If an internal standard is specified in input.txt, the script will calculate calibration curves, uncertainties, confidence intervals, limits of detection (LOD) and limits of quantification (LOQ) using the ratio of analyte peak area to internal‑standard peak area; analyte concentrations are divided by the internal‑standard concentration. Using this internal‑standard method is recommended to compensate for systematic errors such as injection volume, flow‑rate, column condition, or instrument response.

steps.title: Save result tables
steps.instruction: When processing is complete, the script writes a result workbook named “<compound‑name>-Results.xlsx” in the working directory. The file includes columns for sample name, concentration, LOD, LOQ, uncertainty, confidence interval, internal‑standard concentration, internal LOD, internal LOQ, internal uncertainty, internal confidence interval, and T1/T2 identity. Example result files are Atorvastatin‑Results.xlsx, Ibuprofen‑Results.xlsx, and Hydrochlorothiazide‑Results.xlsx.
